mainTopic: Whether a הספד honors the dead, separate graves for executed sinners, and the rule הואיל ונדחה ידחה for קרבנות
overview: The amud opens by asking whether a הספד is held to honor the living or to honor the person who died. The גמרא tries several proofs: חזקיהו's shameful burial of his father, רבי's request not to be eulogized in small towns, and the rules about delaying a burial 'for his honor.' Each of these is pushed aside, until רבי נתן's ברייתא shows that missing a הספד brings atonement to the dead, so the הספד must be the honor of the dead. Next the גמרא explains why executed people get separate graves: a רשע is not buried next to a צדיק, as shown by the man who came back to life in אלישע's grave. Likewise a severe sinner is not buried next to a lighter one, and the number of graveyards, two, is a tradition. Then רבי יוחנן teaches that a קרבן whose owner became a מומר or went insane stays rejected even after he returns (הואיל ונדחה ידחה), and the גמרא explains why both cases were needed. רב יוסף supports this from the קרבנות of an עיר הנדחת. That leads to a debate between אביי and רבא about whether a sinner who is executed gains כפרה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from חזקיהו disgracing his father's burial
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the story of חזקיהו, who dragged his father's bones on a rope bed. If a הספד honors the living, how could he do this?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'In his eyes a vile person is despised.' This is חזקיהו, king of יהודה, who dragged his father's bones on a bed of ropes. If funeral honor is for the living, why did he do this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to try to prove that a הספד is for the honor of the dead, not the living.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיהו gave his wicked father a shameful burial. If the honor belonged to the living, he would have been shaming himself and all of ישראל, which he would have no right to do. So it seems the honor belongs to the dead person, and a wicked dead person can lose it.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source as a proof
In his eyes a vile person is despised (a פסוק in תהלים)
A cheap bed made of ropes, not a proper royal bier
The honor of the living

phrases.english: Come and hear: "In his eyes a vile person is despised"
This is Hezekiah, king of Judah,
who dragged the bones of his father

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier question of whether a הספד is for the living or the dead.
steps.raayaObject: That a הספד and burial honor are for the honor of the dead.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching on the פסוק 'נבזה בעיניו נמאס' about חזקיהו and his father's bones.

steps.title: He did it to bring his father atonement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that חזקיהו shamed his father so that the shame would bring his father כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that his father would have atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof. חזקיהו had a special reason: the shame would bring his father כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed that only the dead person's own honor could be given up. The answer gives another reason for the shameful burial: being disgraced brings atonement for sins. So the story does not prove who the honor belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: Atonement
So that

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתִיהְוֵי לֵיהּ כַּפָּרָה לַאֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: So that there would be atonement for his father,

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּתִיהְוֵי לֵיהּ כַּפָּרָה לַאֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question 'מאי טעמא' from step 1 and so pushes aside the proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from חזקיהו without deciding the main question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The shameful burial can be explained by a different reason, namely atonement for the father.

steps.title: Can the honor of all ישראל be pushed off for one man's atonement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. If the honor belongs to ישראל, how could חזקיהו take it away from them just for his father's atonement?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for his father's atonement, would they push off the honor of ישראל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave, asking whether one person's כפרה is enough reason to take away everyone's honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the honor belongs to the living, then a proper royal funeral was the right of the whole nation. Atoning for one dead king seems too small a reason to cancel the whole people's honor.

keyTerms.meaning: They delay or push off
The honor of the Jewish people

phrases.english: And because of his father's atonement
would they push off the honor of Israel?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשּׁוּם כַּפָּרָה דַּאֲבוּהּ מְשַׁהוּ לֵיהּ לִיקָרָא דְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that חזקיהו acted for his father's atonement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the honor belongs to the living, the whole nation's honor should not be given up for one person's atonement.

steps.title: ישראל agreed to give up their honor
steps.stepSummary: The people themselves were happy to give up their honor so their former king could gain atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: ישראל themselves were glad to give up their honor for his sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the people willingly gave up their own honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the honor belonged to ישראל, they had the right to give it up, and they chose to. So nothing was taken from them against their will, and the proof from חזקיהו stays pushed aside.

keyTerms.meaning: Themselves
It is pleasing to them; they are glad
They give up or forgo

phrases.english: Israel themselves were pleased
to give up their honor for his sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The honor's owners agreed to give it up.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Atonement for one man could not override the honor of the whole nation.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nation willingly gave up its honor, so the honor of the living was not wronged.

steps.title: Proof from רבי: do not eulogize me in the towns
steps.stepSummary: רבי asked not to be eulogized in small towns. If the הספד is for the living, why would he care?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: he said to them, 'Do not eulogize me in the small towns.' If you say the הספד is for the honor of the living, what difference does it make to him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof that a הספד is for the honor of the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי gave instructions about his own הספד. This suggests the הספד is his honor, so he gets to control it. If it belonged to the living, he would have no reason to care where it took place.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not eulogize me
Small towns
What difference does it make to him?

phrases.english: Come and hear: he said to them:
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי יהודה הנשיא, giving instructions before his passing.

phrases.english: Do not eulogize me in the small towns.
And if you say it is for the honor of the living,
what difference does it make to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמַר לָהֶן: אַל תִּסְפְּדוּנִי בָּעֲיָירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof for the same question, after the first proof was pushed aside.
steps.raayaObject: That a הספד is for the honor of the dead.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי's instruction not to be eulogized in the small towns.

steps.title: רבי wanted ישראל to gain more honor
steps.stepSummary: רבי's request was really about the living. He wanted ישראל to be honored more by gathering in the big cities.
steps.simpleTranslation: He held that ישראל would be honored more through him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the second proof by showing that רבי was thinking about the honor of the living.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי cared about the people's honor, not his own. Big gatherings in the large cities would bring more honor to ישראל than many small ones. So his request fits well with the view that a הספד is for the living.

keyTerms.meaning: He held; he was of the opinion
Let them be honored
More

phrases.english: He held: let Israel be honored more through him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 and so pushes aside the proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from רבי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי's instruction can be explained as concern for the honor of the living.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about leaving the dead overnight for his honor
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that leaving a body overnight 'for his honor,' to get a coffin and shrouds, is not a sin. Doesn't 'his honor' mean the dead person's honor?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if he left him overnight for his honor, to bring him a coffin and shrouds, he does not break the prohibition. Doesn't this mean the honor of the dead?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third proof, this time from a משנה, that funeral honor belongs to the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally it is forbidden to leave a body unburied overnight. The משנה allows it 'for his honor,' and the simple reading of 'his' is the dead person. That would show burial honors are for the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: He left him overnight
Coffin
Burial shrouds
He does not break the prohibition
Is it not? (the גמרא suggesting a reading)

phrases.english: Come and hear: if he left him overnight for his honor,
to bring him a coffin and shrouds,
he does not transgress it.
phrases.notes: This is the ban on leaving a body overnight, דברים 21:23.

phrases.english: Is it not for the honor of the dead?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third proof for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That burial honor is for the dead.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that one may leave the body overnight 'לכבודו'.

steps.title: No, 'his honor' means the honor of the living
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'his honor' in the משנה as the honor of the living relative.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means for the honor of the living.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the third proof by reading the word 'his' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לכבודו' does not have to mean the dead person. It can mean the living relative, who would be embarrassed by a poor burial. So the משנה proves nothing either way.

keyTerms.meaning: No: the proof is rejected
For his honor
The living person

steps.whatToRemember: So far, three proofs that a הספד is for the honor of the dead (חזקיהו, רבי, and the משנה) have been pushed aside. Each was explained in a way that fits the view that it is for the honor of the living. Steps 13–14 bring the proof from רבי נתן that finally settles the question.

phrases.english: No, for the honor of the living.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading suggested in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from this משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'לכבודו' can refer to the living relative rather than the dead person.

steps.title: Can the dead be left overnight for the living?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading from step 8. Can a body really be left unburied overnight just for the honor of the living?
steps.simpleTranslation: Can it be that, because of the honor of the living, they leave the dead person unburied overnight?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. Step 8 said 'his honor' means the honor of the living relative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving a body unburied overnight is normally forbidden. If the delay helps only the living, it seems to break the איסור for the sake of someone else. So the step 8 reading now looks hard to accept.

keyTerms.meaning: leaves overnight (a body unburied)
the honor of the living

phrases.english: And because of the honor of the living
they leave the dead person overnight?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל חַי מֵבִית לֵיהּ לְמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the דחיה of step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'his honor' in the משנה means the living relative's honor
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The איסור of leaving a body overnight should not give way for the benefit of someone else.

steps.title: The איסור only applies when the body is disgraced
steps.stepSummary: Yes, it is allowed. The פסוק forbids only cases like a hanging body, where the dead is disgraced. A respectful delay does not disgrace him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. When the Torah said 'His body shall not remain overnight on the tree,' it meant cases like a hanging body, which is a disgrace. Here there is no disgrace, so it is not forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 8. It shows the איסור has a limited scope: it only covers cases where the body is disgraced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about a hanged body, and the גמרא learns that the איסור covers only similar cases of בזיון. Delaying a burial to prepare a dignified funeral is no disgrace. So the delay is allowed even when it is done for the living.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning the Torah
his body shall not remain overnight
similar to
disgrace

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the rule that the איסור of leaving a body overnight depends on whether the body is disgraced.

phrases.english: Yes,
for when the Merciful One said:
"His body shall not remain overnight on the tree,"
it means a case like a hanged body,
which involves disgrace.
But here,
since there is no disgrace in it, it is not forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the scope of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any overnight delay of burial is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a delay that disgraces the dead is forbidden. A respectful delay is allowed, even for the living.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the delay is for the honor of the dead
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows delaying a burial to gather towns, lamenters, a coffin and shrouds. It explains that all this is for the honor of the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If someone left the body overnight for its honor, to announce the death to the towns, to bring lamenters, or to bring a coffin and shrouds, he does not break the איסור. That is because whoever does this does it only for the honor of the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to prove that funeral honors, like a הספד, are for the dead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא says it outright: 'for the honor of the dead.' That seems to beat the step 8 reading, which said 'his honor' meant the living. If funeral preparations are for the dead, the הספד probably is too.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (opens a proof from a source)
women who chant laments at a funeral
burial shrouds
towns

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If he left him overnight for his honor,
to announce his death to the towns,
to bring him lamenters,
to bring him a coffin and shrouds,
he does not transgress because of it,
for whoever does this
does it only for the honor of the dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof against the step 8 reading
steps.raayaObject: That funeral honors, including the הספד, are for the dead

steps.title: The ברייתא means there is no disgrace to the dead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. Whatever is done for the living causes no disgrace to the dead, so it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means: whoever does it for the honor of the living causes no disgrace to the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by explaining the ברייתא's words differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'for the honor of the dead' is read as 'no disgrace to the dead.' The real purpose can still be the honor of the living. This matches the rule from step 10, that only בזיון is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it means (rereads a source)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the ברייתא's words are wrong. It is explaining that they mean 'no disgrace to the dead,' not 'done for the dead.'

phrases.english: This is what it means:
whoever does it for the honor of the living,
there is no disgrace in it for the dead.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: כׇּל הָעוֹשֶׂה לִכְבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל חַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא, not the ברייתא itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof read 'for the honor of the dead' as the purpose of the delay. It can mean only that the delay causes no disgrace to the dead.

steps.title: רבי נתן: missing honor after death brings atonement
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says it is a good sign when a dead person is not eulogized or suffers other dishonor, because he is punished after death. So the הספד must be an honor to the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי נתן says it is a good sign for the dead when he is punished after death. A dead person who was not eulogized or buried, or whom an animal dragged, or on whose bier rain dripped, has a good sign. Learn from this: the הספד is for the honor of the dead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another proof, its fifth, and this one is not pushed away. If missing a הספד is a punishment for the dead, then a הספד must be his honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן counts 'not eulogized' as a punishment that helps the dead person. Missing something can only punish him if that thing honors him. So the הספד is יקרא דשכבי, the honor of the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: a good sign
he is punished
was eulogized
the honor of the dead

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Natan says:
It is a good sign for the dead
when he is punished after death.
A dead person who was not eulogized and not buried,
or whom a wild animal drags,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהָיוּ גְּשָׁמִים מְזַלְּפִין עַל מִטָּתוֹ –
phrases.english: or on whose bier rain was dripping,
this is a good sign for the dead.
Learn from this:
it is for the honor of the dead.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the הספד, which is what the whole discussion has been asking about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new proof after step 11's proof was rejected
steps.raayaObject: That הספד is for the honor of the dead
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נתן's ברייתא: missing a הספד is a punishment that helps the dead

steps.title: Conclusion: הספד honors the dead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the proof. הספד is for the honor of the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it: that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the proof and closes the question about הספד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers were possible, but רבי נתן's teaching settles it. Missing a הספד can only help the dead person as atonement if the הספד was his honor in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from it (here it confirms the proof)

steps.whatToRemember: The final answer is יקרא דשכבי: the הספד is for the honor of the dead, not the living.

phrases.english: Learn from it; so it is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of step 13
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: הספד is יקרא דשכבי, the honor of the dead.

steps.title: Why separate graves for executed people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that executed people were not buried in their family graves. It asks why this is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'They would not bury' him in his family's grave. Why is all this needed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks for the reason behind it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires special court graveyards for people the court executed. The גמרא wants to know why such special arrangements are needed.

phrases.english: "They would not bury..." etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: an executed person was not buried in his family's grave but in a court graveyard.

phrases.english: And why all this?

steps.title: A רשע is not buried next to a צדיק
steps.stepSummary: Because a רשע may not be buried next to a צדיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because we do not bury a wicked person next to a righteous person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the separate graves keep a רשע away from צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An executed person is treated as a רשע. A family grave may hold righteous relatives, so he is buried apart from them.

phrases.english: Because we do not bury

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Separate graves keep a רשע from being buried next to a צדיק.

steps.title: The man thrown into אלישע's grave
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר חנינא brings the source from נביא. A man thrown into אלישע's grave touched his bones and came back to life.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אחא בר חנינא said: From where do we know that a רשע is not buried next to a צדיק? As it says: 'As they were burying a man, they saw a raiding band and threw the man into the grave of אלישע. The man touched the bones of אלישע, came alive, and stood on his feet.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a פסוק as the source for the rule that a רשע is not buried next to a צדיק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads the miracle as a sign that this man was not fit to stay buried next to the צדיק אלישע. So he was brought back to life and left the grave. This shows the rule from step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know?
a raiding band
the נביא, student of אליהו

steps.title: Maybe the man came back to life for a different reason
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests the man was revived to fulfill אלישע's request for a 'double portion', not to keep a רשע away from a צדיק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to him: But perhaps the man came back to life to fulfill 'Let a double portion of your spirit be upon me'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on the proof from step 17. He offers another reason the dead man came back to life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלישע asked אליהו for a double portion of his spirit. אליהו revived one person, so אלישע would need to revive two. If this man was the second one, the miracle proves nothing about burying a רשע next to a צדיק.

phrases.english: But perhaps it was to fulfill

steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The miracle could have happened to complete אלישע's 'double portion', not to keep a רשע away from a צדיק.

steps.title: The man stood up but did not go home
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר חנינא answers from a ברייתא: the man only stood up and did not go home, so his revival was not a real one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, how does that fit what a ברייתא teaches: he stood on his feet, but he did not go to his home?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר חנינא defends his proof. He shows that the man was alive only for a moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the man had been revived to complete אלישע's double portion, he should have lived on. The ברייתא says he stood up and did not go home, so he was revived only to be taken out of the צדיק's grave. The original proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
That which was taught in a ברייתא
He stood up on his feet

phrases.english: He said to him:
If so, how does that fit what was taught:
He stood up on his feet,
but he did not go to his home.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב פפא's alternative and restores the proof from step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a ברייתא that the revival was only momentary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The man was revived as אלישע's second miracle of bringing someone back to life.
steps.terutzMaskana: He did not go home, so it was not a full revival. He was revived only so he would not stay buried next to אלישע.

steps.title: Where was the double portion fulfilled?
steps.stepSummary: If this man does not count, the גמרא asks where אלישע revived a second person.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, about 'Let a double portion', where do you find that he brought a second person to life?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If the dead man in the grave does not count, where did אלישע's double portion come true? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know אלישע revived only one person during his life, the son of the שונמית. Now that the man in the grave is ruled out, the count is missing a second revival.

keyTerms.meaning: Where do you find it?
That he brought to life

phrases.english: But then, "Let a double portion":
where do you find that he brought a second person to life?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא ״וִיהִי נָא פִּי שְׁנַיִם״, הֵיכִי מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 19. Since the man in the grave does not count, the double portion still needs an explanation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which second revival fulfilled אלישע's request for a double portion?

steps.title: Healing נעמן counts as bringing back to life
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that healing נעמן's צרעת counts, because a מצורע is considered like a dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: When he healed נעמן's צרעת, which is equal to death, as it says: 'Let her not be as one dead.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. Curing נעמן was the 'second' revival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה compares a מצורע to a dead person when it speaks about מרים. So healing a מצורע counts like bringing someone back to life. That gives אלישע two revivals, double what אליהו did.

keyTerms.meaning: A skin affliction mentioned in the תורה
The Aramean general healed by אלישע
Considered equal to a dead person

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
That he healed Naaman's tzara'as,
which is considered equal to death,
as it is written: "Let her not be as one dead."
phrases.notes: במדבר 12:12, said about מרים when she had צרעת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שֶׁרִיפֵּא צָרַעַת נַעֲמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Healing נעמן's צרעת counts as a revival, because a מצורע is compared to a dead person.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from אלישע's grave stands: the man was revived only so he would not be buried next to a צדיק. אלישע's double portion was completed by healing נעמן.

steps.title: A very wicked person is not buried next to a less wicked one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה's two graveyards: just as a רשע is not buried next to a צדיק, a more severe sinner is not buried next to a lighter one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as we do not bury a wicked person next to a righteous one, so too we do not bury a very wicked person next to a less wicked one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and explains why there were two separate graveyards for people executed by בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 taught that a רשע is not buried next to a צדיק. The גמרא extends that idea: even among sinners, a severe sinner is kept apart from a lighter one. Those killed by סקילה or שריפה are buried apart from those killed by הרג or חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: A very wicked person, guilty of a severe sin
A less wicked person, guilty of a lighter sin
Next to

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין קוֹבְרִין רָשָׁע אֵצֶל צַדִּיק,
phrases.english: And just as we do not bury a wicked person next to a righteous one,
so too we do not bury a very wicked person
next to a less wicked person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁאֵין קוֹבְרִין רָשָׁע אֵצֶל צַדִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's burial rules and extends the principle of step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A severe sinner is not buried next to a lighter sinner. This explains the משנה's two graveyards.

steps.title: Why not four graveyards?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if sinners are separated by severity, there should be four graveyards, one for each type of execution.
steps.simpleTranslation: So let them set up four graveyards!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four court deaths, and each has a different level of severity. If we separate by severity, four graveyards would make more sense than two.

keyTerms.meaning: So let them set up
Graveyards

phrases.english: So let them set up four graveyards!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the logic of step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason for two graveyards (separating by severity)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If severity decides the burial, each of the four court deaths should have its own graveyard.

steps.title: Two graveyards is a tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the number two is a received tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two graveyards: this is learned as a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The number of graveyards was handed down, not worked out by logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of separating by severity explains why there is more than one graveyard. The exact number, two, comes from tradition, so we do not make four.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned as a tradition

phrases.english: Two graveyards:
this is learned as a tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separating by severity should lead to four graveyards.
steps.terutzMaskana: There are only two, because that is the tradition.
steps.whatToRemember: Sinners executed by בית דין are buried in two graveyards. The reason is to keep severe sinners apart from lighter ones, and the number two is a tradition.

steps.title: A קרבן pushed off stays pushed off
steps.stepSummary: עולא says in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone set aside a חטאת for eating חלב, then became a מומר and later came back, the קרבן stays rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone ate חלב and set aside a קרבן, then became a מומר and returned, since the קרבן was pushed off, it stays pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new teaching. It is about a קרבן that could not be brought for a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מומר cannot bring a קרבן. While the owner was a מומר, his קרבן became unfit. Even after he does תשובה, the קרבן does not become fit again, because once it was pushed off it stays pushed off.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat
Became a מומר (left the Jewish faith)
Came back, regretted
Since it was pushed off, it stays pushed off

steps.confusionAlert: The rule is about the קרבן, not the person. His תשובה is accepted, but this particular animal can no longer be brought.

phrases.english: Ulla said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
If one ate forbidden fat and set aside an offering,
and then he became an apostate and came back,
since it was pushed off, it stays pushed off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the graveyard discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרבן that became unfit while its owner was a מומר stays unfit even after he does תשובה (הוֹאִיל וְנִדְחָה, יִדָּחֶה).
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle that something pushed off stays pushed off (דחוי) shows up in many places in ש״ס, and the גמרא will build on it next.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's parallel rule for an owner who became insane
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if someone set aside a חטאת for eating חלב, then became insane and later recovered, the קרבן stays rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone ate חלב, set aside a קרבן, went insane, and then became sane again, the קרבן was pushed off, so it stays pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second statement of רבי יוחנן with the same rule as before, but now the owner became insane instead of becoming a מומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 the owner was rejected because he became a מומר. Here he is rejected because a שוטה cannot bring a קרבן. Even after he recovers, the animal stays rejected under the same rule: הואיל ונדחה ידחה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated: another teaching that says the same idea
He became insane (a שוטה)
He became sane again
Since it was pushed off, it stays pushed off

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said that Rabbi Abbahu said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If one ate forbidden fat and set aside an offering,
and then became insane, and later became sane again,
since it was pushed off, it stays pushed off.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel ruling by the same אמורא, applying the rule of step 25 to an insane owner
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חטאת whose owner went insane and then recovered stays rejected: הואיל ונדחה ידחה.

steps.title: Why the מומר case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that from the מומר case alone we might think the rule applies only when the owner rejected himself on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both rulings were needed. If we had only the first one, we might say the reason is that the מומר pushed himself away by his own choice. But someone who became insane got pushed off on his own, so we might say he is like a person who is asleep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to explain why רבי יוחנן needed to teach both cases. Here it shows what we might have wrongly thought if we only had the מומר case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מומר chose to leave, so it makes sense that his קרבן is rejected. An insane person did not choose anything. We might compare him to someone asleep, whose קרבן is not rejected just because he cannot act for a while.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was necessary: both teachings are needed
With his own hands: by his own active choice
On its own, without the person doing anything
He is like a person who is asleep

phrases.english: And it was necessary to teach both,
for if he had taught us only the first case,
phrases.notes: The first case is the מומר from step 25.

phrases.english: I would say that is because he pushed himself away with his own hands,
but this one, who was pushed off by itself,
I would say he is like someone who is asleep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ruling of step 26 adds something beyond step 25
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the מומר case alone we could not learn the insanity case, because the insane person did not reject himself by choice.

steps.title: Why the insanity case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: From the insanity case alone we might think the rule applies only when the owner has no power to come back. A מומר can come back whenever he wants, so we need both teachings.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we had only this case of insanity, we might say the reason is that he has no power to get better on his own. But the מומר can choose to come back at any time, so we might say his קרבן is not rejected. So both teachings were necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא by showing the opposite side. Each case teaches something the other could not, so both are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The insane person cannot fix his situation, so his rejection is strong. The מומר could do תשובה at any moment, so we might think his קרבן is only on hold. Since each case has its own reason to be lenient, רבי יוחנן had to teach both.

keyTerms.meaning: It is in his power to come back
I would say not: I would have thought the rule does not apply

steps.whatToRemember: A צריכא shows that two rulings that look the same each teach something new. Here, choice versus no choice, and the power to return versus no power to return.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only here,
I would say that is because it is not in his power to come back,
but there, where it is in his power to come back,
I would say it is not rejected. So both were necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכא begun in step 27
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both cases are needed: the מומר case covers someone who could return, and the insanity case covers someone who did not choose to be rejected.

steps.title: רב יוסף brings support from עיר הנדחת
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף proves the rule of הואיל ונדחו ידחו from a teaching about altar animals belonging to the people of an עיר הנדחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: We also learned this. If there were holy items in the city, altar animals must be left to die, and items for Temple upkeep are redeemed. We asked: why must they die? Once the people are killed, they have atonement, so let the animals be brought on the altar! Isn't the reason that we say: since they were pushed off, they stay pushed off?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings an earlier teaching that supports רבי יוחנן's rule that a rejected קרבן stays rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the owners served עבודה זרה, their קרבנות could not be brought. After they are executed they have atonement and would be fit again, yet the animals still must die. The best explanation is הואיל ונדחו ידחו, the same rule רבי יוחנן taught.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it: an earlier source already says this
Items holy for the altar (animals for קרבנות)
Items holy for the upkeep of the בית המקדש
They are redeemed: bought back so they lose their holiness
Atonement
To the Most High: offered on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יוחנן's rule is not new. An older teaching already depends on the idea that something pushed off stays pushed off.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: We too have learned this:
If there were holy items in it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is an עיר הנדחת, a city that turned to עבודה זרה and is destroyed.

phrases.english: items holy for the altar must be left to die,
items holy for Temple upkeep are redeemed.
And we discussed it: why must they die?
Once the people were killed, they have atonement,
so let the animals go up to the Most High!
Is it not because we say:
since they were pushed off, they stay pushed off?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that supports רבי יוחנן's rule from steps 25-26
steps.raayaObject: The rule הואיל ונדחה ידחה for a קרבן whose owner was temporarily unfit
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching that altar animals of an עיר הנדחת must die even though their executed owners have atonement

steps.title: אביי asks: does a wicked person who dies get atonement?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף's proof by asking whether someone who dies while still wicked really gets כפרה. He says no.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do you really think that someone who dies in his wickedness gets atonement? Someone who dies in his wickedness does not get atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the assumption behind רב יוסף's proof. He says that a person who dies without doing תשובה does not get כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's proof from עיר הנדחת depended on the idea that the wicked owners had gained כפרה. אביי denies that idea, so the proof loses its footing. He backs up his claim in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Dies while still in his wickedness, without doing תשובה
Atonement, forgiveness for sin
Do you really hold? A question that challenges an assumption

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Do you hold

phrases.aramaic: מֵת מִתּוֹךְ רִשְׁעוֹ הָוְיָא לֵיהּ כַּפָּרָה?
phrases.english: that one who dies in his wickedness gets atonement?
One who dies in his wickedness
does not get atonement,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the hidden assumption in רב יוסף's proof from step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's assumption that the wicked owners in עיר הנדחת achieved כפרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person who dies without תשובה gets no כפרה, so the assumption the proof relies on is false.

steps.title: Proof from a priest who may not bury an apostate parent
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves his point from רב שמעיה's ברייתא: a כהן may not become טמא for a parent who left the ways of the community.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב שמעיה taught: You might think that even if his parents left the ways of the community, the כהן should still become impure to bury them. So the verse says "among his people", which means only for someone who acts like his people.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא to support his claim. A כהן may become טמא only for a relative who lived like a Jew, not for one who left the community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the apostate parent's death had wiped away his sin, he would count as "among his people" again and the כהן could bury him. Since the כהן still may not, death alone did not bring כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought, which sets up a wrong idea for the פסוק to reject
Separated from the ways of the community, meaning left Jewish practice
He should become ritually impure, here a כהן becoming impure to bury a relative
"Among his people", the words the proof is built on

phrases.english: as Rav Shemaya taught:
One might think that even if his parents separated themselves
from the ways of the community, he should become impure for them?
phrases.notes: "He" is a כהן, who normally may become impure only to bury close relatives.

phrases.english: The verse says: "Among his people"
meaning, for one who acts the way his people act.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for אביי's claim in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one who dies in his wickedness gets no כפרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב שמעיה's ברייתא on ויקרא 21:1: a כהן may not become impure for a parent who left the community.

steps.title: רבא: being killed is different from dying naturally
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a sinner who dies naturally gets no כפרה, but a sinner who is executed does get כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Are you comparing someone killed in his wickedness to someone who died in his wickedness? One who died in his wickedness died a normal death, so he gets no atonement. One who was killed in his wickedness did not die a normal death, so he does get atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רב יוסף's proof. He says אביי's source deals with a natural death, but the people of עיר הנדחת were executed, and that is a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא accepts אביי's rule but limits it to a natural death. An unnatural death, such as execution, itself brings כפרה even without תשובה. So the owners in עיר הנדחת did get כפרה, and רב יוסף's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Killed while still in his wickedness
Are you comparing? A way of saying the two cases are not alike
In its normal way, here meaning a natural death

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not disagree with רב שמעיה's ברייתא. He agrees that a natural death without תשובה brings no כפרה. He only says execution is different.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Are you comparing
one who was killed in his wickedness
to one who died in his wickedness?
One who died in his wickedness,
since he died in the normal way,
does not get atonement.
One who was killed in his wickedness,
since he did not die in the normal way,
does get atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: מִי קָא מְדַמֵּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by separating execution from natural death.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any wicked person who dies without תשובה lacks כפרה, so the עיר הנדחת owners had none.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a natural death lacks כפרה. Execution itself brings כפרה.

steps.title: Proof from תהלים: the executed are called "Your servants"
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a פסוק in תהלים that calls killed sinners "Your servants", which shows their death gave them כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is true, as it is written: "A song of אסף. God, nations came into Your inheritance, they made Your holy Temple impure... They gave the corpses of Your servants as food for the birds of the sky, the flesh of Your pious ones to the animals of the earth." What is "Your servants" and what is "Your pious ones"? Isn't it that "Your pious ones" means truly pious people, while "Your servants" means people who had earlier deserved punishment, but because they were killed, the פסוק calls them "Your servants"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא supports his distinction with a פסוק. The פסוק names two groups of people who were killed, and he explains the difference between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Your pious ones" were righteous all along. "Your servants" were sinners who deserved punishment. Yet once they were killed, the פסוק honors them as God's servants, which shows that being killed gave them כפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Know that it is so, which introduces supporting evidence
Your servants, here sinners who gained כפרה by being killed
Your pious ones, people who were truly righteous
Liable to punishment

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule: a sinner who dies naturally gets no כפרה, but a sinner who is killed gets כפרה even without תשובה. The proof is that תהלים calls killed sinners "Your servants".
steps.whyThisMatters: This distinction keeps רב יוסף's proof for הואיל ונדחו ידחו alive, because it means the owners in עיר הנדחת did gain כפרה.

phrases.english: Know that this is so, as it is written:
A song of Asaf.
God, nations have come into Your inheritance;
they have made Your holy Temple impure, etc.
They have given the corpses of Your servants
as food for the birds of the sky,
the flesh of Your pious ones to the animals of the earth."
What is "Your servants" and what is "Your pious ones"?
Isn't it that "Your pious ones" means truly pious people,
and "Your servants" means those who were deserving punishment at first,
but since they were killed,
the verse calls them "Your servants"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's distinction from step 32 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: A sinner who is killed gains כפרה even without תשובה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 79:1–2: killed sinners are called "עבדיך", next to the truly righteous "חסידיך".

steps.title: אביי begins a new challenge to רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts to answer רבא with his own "are you comparing" question. The rest of his words continue on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are you comparing...
steps.whatsHappening: This is only the opening line of a new challenge. The גמרא is setting up אביי's next move, and the full question continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי uses the same words רבא just used, "מי קא מדמית". He is about to argue that רבא's proof from תהלים compares two cases that are not alike.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Are you comparing...

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מִי קָא מְדַמֵּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens אביי's pushback against רבא's proof from תהלים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's proof from the פסוק in תהלים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case in the פסוק may not be comparable to the case under discussion. The full argument continues past this section.
